schema: M36 coverage sweep: one record per runnable case; verdict CLEAN|SKIPS(n)|ERROR|TIMEOUT|CRASH as defined in sweep_coverage.py docstring; ranked_gaps counts cases_using (deck contains the unsupported family) and cases_blocking (family is a hard physics skip in that case's run). parse_error_signatures ranks the caught reader failures ('** ERROR while reading /X' — port parse bugs on real decks, distinct from clean unsupported-keyword skips and from rc!=0 crashes, of which there were none). M37 rerun: identical driver/corpus/verdict definitions as M36; adds delta_vs_m36 with the verdict migration matrix, per-signature and per-gap deltas. M38 rerun: identical driver/corpus/verdict definitions as M36/M37; adds delta_vs_m37 with the verdict migration matrix, per-signature/per-gap deltas, and an error_class_delta so any NEW error class or crash is surfaced loudly in delta_vs_m37.new_bugs. M39 rerun: identical driver/corpus/verdict definitions as M36/M37/M38; adds delta_vs_m38 with the verdict migration matrix, per-signature/per-gap deltas, an error_class_delta, and a new_bugs section reporting the fate of the M39 target bug families (SKEW/FRAME via gap_delta; degenerate bricks + the small-bug pack via error classes) and surfacing any NEW error class, crash, timeout or driver-fail LOUDLY. M41 rerun: identical driver/corpus/verdict definitions as M36..M40; adds delta_vs_m40 with the verdict migration matrix, per-signature/per-gap deltas, an error_class_delta, and a new_bugs section; adds a top-level shell_dispatch section that joins the per-case Ishell-dispatch ground truth (QBAT/QEPH routing counts harvested from the port listings) against the M40->M41 migration to prove deck-by-deck that the new shell element-technology dispatch is starter-verdict-neutral. Any NEW error class, crash, timeout, driver-fail, or shell-dispatch regression is surfaced LOUDLY.

shell_dispatch.note: M41 introduced the /PROP/SHELL Ishell dispatch in the STARTER (_dispatch_shell_formulations): Ishell=12 -> QBAT kernel, Ishell=22/23/24 -> QEPH kernel, split out of the generic Belytschko-Tsay group. Decks with those Ishell values ran on the BT kernel as a fallback in M40 and now take the new code path. This section is the deck-by-deck proof that the split is verdict-neutral. Ground truth is the port's own routing INFO line ('N /SHELL ELEMENT(S) ROUTED TO THE {QBAT|QEPH} FORMULATION KERNEL (Ishell dispatch)'), an M41-only emission, harvested from the port-written *_0000.out listings into dispatch_map.json immediately after the sweep.
shell_dispatch.verdict: PASS: every dispatch-firing deck kept its exact M40 verdict AND its full (verdict, hard_skips, error_messages, parse_errors, n_skipped_families) record byte-for-byte; the Ishell dispatch and the QBAT/QEPH kernels are starter-verdict-neutral while actively exercising the new path on 160 decks.

delta_vs_m40.note: M40 -> M41 delta. Same corpus (529 runnable official decks), same driver (sweep_coverage.run_case), same verdict definitions, same 120 s per-deck timeout, same 6-worker method, no backend pin (the sweep runs only the STARTER, whose verdicts are backend-independent). M41's landed work is SHELL element technology: the starter-side /PROP/SHELL Ishell dispatch that routes Ishell=12 to the QBAT kernel and Ishell=22/23/24 to the QEPH kernel out of the generic Belytschko-Tsay group, the QBAT/QEPH branches in resolve_surfaces, the _EGROUP_FAMILIES SHEL widening, and the BT rate-kinematics fix. Because the dispatch runs in the STARTER, this sweep exercises it directly (see shell_dispatch: it fired on 160 decks). Any migration is reported below; any regression / new error class / crash / timeout / driver-fail is surfaced LOUDLY in new_bugs and (for shell decks) shell_dispatch. The user's 12-process MPI engine job may have been running during the sweep (20-core box, 6 workers); per-case elapsed is retained so contended records are visible, and starter runs are short enough (batch wall 82 s for all 529) that contention cannot manufacture a TIMEOUT.

m40_flagged_fates.class: RBODY mass-accumulation ('rigid body has no mass') -- resolved earlier, confirm the shell-group split did not disturb it
degenerate brick (penta/pyramid) rejection ('degenerated brick with N distinct nodes') -- closed in M39, confirm
MAT null-density false-positive on /MAT/LAW0 VOID ('zero or missing initial density') -- resolved in M39, confirm
/PROP/SPRING pretensioner mass requirement ('mass must be') -- resolved in M39, confirm
RBODY node-overlap strictness ('already belong to another rigid body') -- resolved in M39, confirm
shell property / element-group errors mentioning SHELL -- would surface a broken Ishell split

new_bugs.note: m40_flagged_fates reports the fate of the earlier-resolved error classes, tracked so the M41 shell-group split (which edits Model.shells* handling adjacent to element-group and surface resolution) cannot silently re-regression them. new_error_classes lists every normalized error-message signature that appears in M41 but not M40; is_regression is True iff any affected deck was CLEAN/SKIPS in M40. new_crashes/timeouts/driver_fails are LOUD because M40 had zero of each; any entry is a regression. The shell-dispatch-specific proof is in the top-level shell_dispatch section.
